(0, 'Furniture candidate construction derives a group ID from seed, anchor kind and ID, group kind and slot; it retains the anchor, recipe keys, offsets and checked footprint. Placement rejects candidates for unsupported scope, overlap, market containment, unusable or steep ground, or any unsupported item. Only after all items succeed does it insert occupancy, retain the group ID, kind, anchor and footprint, and append instances to playable or distant lists. Each generated instance derives its ID from the group ID and item index and retains the outdoor group ID, key, checked position and orientation. This is a scoped source trace; identity collision, all producers, interior and receiver contracts remain open.')
(1, 'The server spawns playable furniture instances with their retained SceneFurniture identity and transform; its add observer marks them replicated, adds a static body and reconstructs a compound collider from the same FurnitureKey recipe. Group metadata is retained separately for vista/reconnect. Distant instances are kept as SceneVistaFurniture and copied into the vista bundle without colliders or per-entity replication. The client recreates their presentation roots from the bundle and resolves each key into cached recipe mesh batches; playable SceneFurniture is registered for once-only replication. This preserves the intentional playable versus distant authority distinction for the inspected path, without qualifying every serializer, native collider implementation or malformed recipe case.')
(2, 'Interior furnishing maps generator errors to SceneInputError::Interior with the building ID. Installation converts each placement to a scene-space instance using building origin, orientation and floor height, retains FurnitureLocation::Interior with building, room and storey, and derives the instance ID from those identities plus local position, facing and kind. It appends instances one at a time before appending the InteriorBuildingLayout.
